newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse just lower, but resilient.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse just lower, but resilient.

text.p: German shares eased slightly in bourse trade on Wednesday, their pace checked a bit by overnight weakness on Wall Street, but they were still resilient after the recent run-up to record levels.
The 30-share DAX index ended down 2.38 points at 2,625.70 after hovering in a six-point range throughout the session.
Dealers said there was no great selling pressure and the market was winding down after a turbulent start to the week and ahead of key German economic data expected later this week.
"People are drawing some breath after Monday," said a Frankfurt dealer, referring to the market's record heights reached earlier this week.
Current levels remained firm and the stable dollar was supporting the market, dealers said.
Looking ahead, eyes would be on the influential Ifo business climate index report which was expected to be released on Thursday. Last month's surprising jump in the index took markets by surprise.
The Bundesbank's fortnightly meeting would also be a focus of attention on Thursday, although market players are not expecting any change in interest rates.
"We all know it's illogical but we will be watching out for the Bundesbank as usual," said a dealer.
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas AG came under some pressure to drop 4.70 marks to 133.80 as short-covering kicked in after a period of interest in the stock after the Olympics.
